title: Story 6-5 Review: Implement one-to-many matching OR update acceptance criteria
description:
**Code Review Finding #6 - HIGH**

AC6.5-03 requires "auto-suggest matches" but one-to-many matching is not implemented.

**Story file confirms this is incomplete:**
```
[ ] Handle one-to-many matching
```
Location: docs/sprint-artifacts/stories/6-5-manual-bank-reconciliation.md line 173

**Use case:** 
Bank consolidates multiple deposits into a single line (e.g., "Daily deposits: 5,000,000"). The GL has multiple individual receipt entries. Users need to match one bank line to many GL entries.

**Current behavior:** Only 1:1 matching is supported.

**Required changes:**
1. Update DTO to support `List<UUID> matchedVoucherIds` instead of single UUID
2. Add UI to select multiple ledger transactions
3. Update matching algorithm to suggest grouped matches when amounts sum correctly
4. Update ReconciliationMatcherService.manualMatch() to accept multiple vouchers

**Alternative:** If this is out of scope, remove "one-to-many" from AC6.5-03 and document as future enhancement.

title: Story 6-5 Review: Replace in-memory error report storage with Redis/DB
description:
**Code Review Finding #7 - MODERATE**

Error report storage uses in-memory ConcurrentHashMap which has several production issues.

**Location:** StatementImportServiceImpl.java lines 78-79

```java
// In-memory error report storage (would use Redis/DB in production)
private final Map<String, List<ImportErrorDTO>> errorReportStore = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
```

**Problems:**
1. **Data loss on restart:** All error reports lost when server restarts
2. **No TTL:** Reports never expire, potential memory leak over time
3. **No multi-instance support:** With multiple backend instances, user might get "report not found" if routed to different instance
4. **No persistence:** Cannot audit what errors occurred in past imports

**Recommendations:**
1. Use Redis with TTL (e.g., 1 hour expiry)
2. Or persist to database with cleanup job
3. Include cleanup in downloadErrorReport() to free memory after download

**Workaround for MVP:** Add a comment with FIXME tag and create follow-up ticket for production deployment.

title: Story 6-5 Review: Implement actual date format detection instead of stub
description:
**Code Review Finding #5 - HIGH**

The `detectDateFormat()` method is a stub that always returns "yyyy-MM-dd" regardless of actual file content.

**Location:** StatementImportServiceImpl.java lines 480-483

```java
private String detectDateFormat(InputStream inputStream, String fileName, String dateColumn) {
    // Default format
    return "yyyy-MM-dd";  // ← ALWAYS returns default!
}
```

**Problem:** Vietnamese bank statements commonly use:
- `dd/MM/yyyy` (Vietcombank, BIDV)
- `dd-MM-yyyy` (Techcombank)
- `MM/dd/yyyy` (some international banks)

**Impact:** Users will get parsing errors for non-ISO date formats unless they manually specify the format in the column mapping wizard.

**Suggested implementation:**
1. Read first 5-10 non-empty date values from the file
2. Try parsing with common patterns in order of likelihood
3. Return the first pattern that successfully parses all samples
4. Fall back to "yyyy-MM-dd" if no pattern matches
